result.decision_rationale: All four round-six corrections are verified. Three requirements remain open. The multi-launch runner checks for competing sessions only once, the new item-damage failure omits required diagnostic context, and the saved-spear check predates the change to registered item damage.

The controller receipt at 7f44ae6e7415 records successful production compilation and 29 of 29 selected elven-branched-spear tests in 1.8 seconds. The transcript also records the guarded push of that commit.

The developer transcript identifies the tested ZIP as 83c936d58bdda1e7e09b6988e612c4550287d8b0d2ba212a281001e1965fcb75 and the loaded product DLL as 5e7d69d17e9dfd5509c4b32e0ef40cedfed4c12e8d13a1ea5df1ccd33ee3fe7d. X6 passed 3 launches, C6 passed 3, R6 passed 2 and S6 passed 12. Each session summary recorded registry restoration and unchanged owner saves and installation.

required_gaps: A focused contention check covering a peer appearing between native launches and safe recovery while that peer is active.
A bounded item-level BaseDamage failure showing the donor comparison and the implicated getter's patch owners.
A fresh-process observation of effective damage on the inventory spear loaded with the corrected product.
source_inspection_only: The runner's behavior when a foreign process or lock appears after session preflight, including the final registry restoration path.
The diagnostic emitted by DamageProblem for a wrong or throwing item-level getter. X6-1 exercised successful normalization of the donor override.
The strict origin-creation and ownership paths still require the token, and the summoning menu hook checks for a published variants component before applying its layout.

findings.actual: Assert-LcPreflight runs once before staging. The loop calls Start-LcKingmakerCopy for each launch without rechecking the process or foreign locks. The finalizer waits up to 60 seconds and then calls Restore-LcRegistry even if a Kingmaker process is still running. The session owns loader-compat.lock while the generic runtime launcher uses compatibility.lock.
findings.blocking_rationale: On the shared DATA host, a later launch can overlap another session and cleanup can overwrite that session's game settings. The successful restoration fields describe the completed runs and do not exercise this contention path.
findings.expected: Each fresh launch verifies that the host is available. Registry restoration proceeds under transaction ownership once the host is safe.
findings.requested_correction: Use the shared runtime ownership mechanism for the transaction and check for a foreign game or configured lock immediately before each launch. If contention prevents safe restoration, retain the journal and ownership information for recovery.
findings.requested_evidence: Use disposable process and lock fixtures to introduce a peer after launch one. Show that launch two is withheld, registry restoration waits for a safe boundary, and normal completion or recovery releases the owned state.
findings.title: Later native launches can proceed after another session takes the host
findings.trigger: Another Kingmaker process starts or a sibling lab acquires a runtime lock after the spear session's initial preflight.

findings.actual: DamageProblem returns overrideDice, baseDamage and expectedBaseDamage. It has no donor input or patch-owner lookup. A getter exception contributes its full message directly to the startup error, bypassing the type-profile diagnostic's length bound.
findings.blocking_rationale: The new item-level predicate can abort the same blueprint initialization transaction. Its failure omits the information the mission requires to diagnose a patched getter.
findings.expected: The failure identifies the item and predicate, expected and actual damage, the corresponding donor value and relevant getter patch owners in one bounded diagnostic.
findings.requested_correction: Give the item-damage failure the same bounded diagnostic treatment as the type predicates. Capture donor damage as comparison context, preserve the owned failure if the donor read throws, and report patch owners for BlueprintItemWeapon.BaseDamage.
findings.requested_evidence: Use a control that changes or throws from BaseDamage on one registered spear item while its weapon type stays correct. Record one failure identifying the item, expected and actual result, donor result and harness patch owner.
findings.title: Item-damage failures omit the donor value and getter patch owners
findings.trigger: The registered spear type passes its profile check, but BlueprintItemWeapon.BaseDamage returns the wrong dice or throws for an owned item.

findings.actual: Persistence session P ran on 8ee7eabaeda0, before the item override was cleared. Its reload probe reads spear.Blueprint.Type for damage. X6-1 checks the corrected BlueprintItemWeapon.BaseDamage through a blueprint lookup, without reloading a saved inventory spear.
findings.blocking_rationale: Round six changed construction of the released item referenced by saves. The earlier reload and the current blueprint lookup leave the affected saved-item observation uncovered.
findings.expected: A fresh process running the corrected product loads the released spear and observes 1d8 through the loaded item's blueprint, alongside the established disabled-publication controls.
findings.requested_correction: Extend the existing reload observation to read the inventory spear's BlueprintItemWeapon.BaseDamage and override flag. Exercise that focused load on the corrected package using an authorized disposable fixture.
findings.requested_evidence: Record the package and DLL identities, loaded save identity, released spear GUID, override flag and effective item damage with Gunslinger disabled. Include the existing battered-owner, price and restoration results.
findings.title: The fresh-process reload does not cover the corrected spear item damage
findings.trigger: An existing save containing the released foundation spear is loaded after the change to item-level damage overrides.

findings.actual: Section 4.2 says src/ and tests/ are unchanged from 18361607eda8 to the final candidate. Git shows four changed files across those directories. Section 3.1 also illustrates the current message with 17 checks although the product now runs 18.

findings.expected: Historical source-equivalence statements name their endpoint, and the present-tense diagnostic example uses the current count.
findings.requested_correction: Scope the round-five comparison to its checkpoint and update the current diagnostic example to 18. Preserve the 17-check quotations from earlier runs.
findings.requested_evidence: A text check against Git history and the X6 diagnostic is sufficient.
findings.title: Two historical statements still read as claims about the final candidate

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: Foundation, named and progression construction clear the inherited dice override and validate effective item damage. X6-1 completed the item-API assertions for the 2d6 native donor, 1d8 foundation spear and 1d8 Boughkeeper.

The registered type now checks the live Enchantments collection against the movement enchantment by object identity. X6-2 recorded the intact backing field, empty getter result, harness patch owner, exactly one profile failure and successful selector restoration.
The validator checks GetSubCategories separately from HasSubCategory. X6-3 recorded Simple only in the returned list, one list failure naming both patch owners, and successful selector restoration.

The opening now leads with product dfc86851a8 and package revision 0a926ce1d8bd, then identifies the round-five and round-two artifacts. Those identities match Git history and the recorded package hashes.

Ordinary weapon tooltips retain native prices after failed startup. With the available reporter mods and settings, a new sorcerer opened the creature menu and summoned the selected Fire Beetle.
